cards.heading: Then, making them
cards.body: I got hooked on PC games when I was seven. By eight, I was writing little games of my own.
facts: I still play on PC, PlayStation, and Switch. I love Pokemon. Growing up has done very little to fix any of this.

cards.heading: C, C++, and an audience
cards.body:
The lucky part was finding my thing early: computer science and C/C++.

House captain introduced me to leadership, public speaking, and debate, irrespective of how many people wanted to hear my opinions.

cards.heading: Dengue, right before finals
cards.body:
A few weeks before my Class 12 final exams, complicated dengue put me in hospital for a month.

I still finished Class 12 in the national top 0.01% for CS and entered the BE in Computer Engineering at Goa Engineering College, Goa University.

Mosquitoes and I have not reconciled.

cards.heading: The syllabus had competition
cards.body:
College was my first time living on my own. A lot of growing up happened here.

I became department general secretary.

PyCon introduced me to Python.

My Zuari internship introduced me to enterprise software: an on-premise SAP data center.

I presented a paper on securing voice and video calls.

Hackathons became minibosses: seven wins in four years, plus national top ten in the 24-hour IEEE Xtreme.

I finished among the top of my class. This was becoming a bit of a trend.

chapters.heading: Six months. A lot of Java.

cards.heading: A proper training program
cards.body:
HSDI (HSBC Software Development India) took me to Pune for six months of Java training. I finished, you guessed it, at the top of the class.

C/C++, Python, now Java. Gotta catch 'em all. I went on to lead five developers building banking utilities.

chapters.heading: Surely a script can do this.

cards.heading: Bored, not done
cards.body:
Banking red tape blocked new work, so I automated mine and built apps like TasKing.

My Lean Six Sigma Green Belt project saved over 2,000 hours.

Hungry to learn more, I looked at US universities and took GRE and TOEFL. I did really well. Again.

cards.heading: Prof. Paul, 110%, and competitive homework
cards.body:
SJSU was affordable, challenging, and exactly what I needed. In Professor Paul Nguyen's class, I scored 110%, the maximum possible, and was his only student to do it.

I was promptly made his TA, automating grading and building student leaderboards.

I also built SpartanBot, an Alexa-powered campus chatbot, and placed second at PayPal's Opportunity Hack.

chapters.period_label: Jun-Aug 2018 / Google Hardware/Nest, during my MS
chapters.heading: Good news, everyone!

cards.heading: Google, during my master's
cards.body:
Google Hardware/Nest felt different: cooler products and a culture with matching whimsy.

I built tools and infrastructure for developers, with feedback coming straight back to me. This was the work I wanted.

Imposter syndrome was real, but so was learning from engineers far better than me. Intimidating, intoxicating, addictive. I left wanting more.
facts: I loved choosing whatever language fit, digging into infrastructure and deployment, and hearing directly from developers. You never have to wonder whether they have feedback.

cards.heading: And room to explore
cards.body:
I joined Salesforce in 2019 and moved to San Francisco.

I automated months of manual Chat release prep down to minutes and helped move the monolith from data centers to AWS.

Full-time work had no internship end date. I had room to explore, surrounded by smart people.

cards.heading: Finding a new cadence
cards.body: COVID forced a sustainable new cadence of contribution without burning myself out.

cards.heading: Reliability, APIs, then LLMs
cards.body:
On Einstein Bots, I improved CI/CD and monitoring, including Argo CD, and got the service to 99.99% availability. I also worked on its public API and seamlessly migrated 100% of customer traffic from Heroku to multisubstrate public-cloud instances.

As part of the API work, I contributed to the public Slack connector. Useful, but not the main quest.

When LLMs arrived, I pivoted to Einstein Copilot: a platform for talking to a configurable AI agent inside Salesforce.
facts: Off the clock: guitar, drones, golf, cooking, cocktails, karting, sim racing, dogs, blogging, and poetry. Also lists. You may have noticed.

cards.heading: Principal, not finished
cards.body:
Next came a platform where Salesforce customers could build their own agents. Basic topics and actions grew into the Atlas Reasoning Engine and AgentScript, making agent behavior more deterministic in an LLM world.

Now we add voice, MCP, native context, memory, an agentic runtime, async processing, and long-running turns, actions, and sessions.

Connecting Salesforce CRM data to the agent platform has been a fun place to work, learn, and grow. I also build context-aware DevOps tools for my team: a work assistant and coding harness. My enthusiasm, drive, and passion are at an all-time high.

achievements.heading: Agentforce products and developer tools
achievements.body: I help grow Agentforce's Atlas Reasoning Engine and AgentScript with voice, MCP, native context, memory, agentic runtime, async work, and long-running turns, actions, and sessions. I also build context-aware DevOps tools for my team.

achievements.heading: DevOpsing the house
achievements.body: My homelab runs Home Assistant and a media stack. My OpenClaw and Hermes agents maintain each other; Morpheus keeps credential access behind human approval.

achievements.heading: I'm 40% PLA.
achievements.body: MakerWorld, Bambu Studio, and Autodesk Fusion replaced Amazon Prime. Why buy it when I can spend six hours making it?

achievements.heading: Senior, Lead, Principal
achievements.body: Senior in October 2020, Lead in August 2023, Principal in February 2025.

achievements.body: I got Bots to 99.99% availability through CI/CD, Argo CD, and monitoring; worked on its public API; and seamlessly migrated 100% of customer traffic from Heroku to multisubstrate public cloud. The API work included my Slack connector contribution.

achievements.body: I helped turn months of Chat release prep into minutes, then helped move the monolith from data centers to AWS.

achievements.heading: 110%, then Prof. Paul's TA
achievements.body: I was Prof. Paul's only student to score the maximum 110%. Then I became his TA and built a Docker/Python autograder and live leaderboards.

achievements.heading: SpartanBot and a PayPal hackathon
achievements.body: I built an Alexa campus chatbot, then placed second at PayPal's Opportunity Hack with another Alexa project for San Jose.

achievements.heading: TasKing, Green Belt, and CI/CD
achievements.body: I built TasKing in Java/Swing. A separate Green Belt project saved 2,000+ hours; separate CI/CD work cut time to market by 25%.

achievements.heading: Caught the Java bug
achievements.body: At HSDI (HSBC Software Development India), I finished first in six-month Java training, led five developers, and became its youngest Rising Star nominee at 20.

achievements.heading: GEC: degree, leadership, and a paper
achievements.body: I finished my BE in Computer Engineering with a 3.7 GPA, served as department general secretary, and presented a call-security paper.

achievements.heading: The miniboss collection
achievements.body: Seven wins in four years. The final miniboss was a national top-ten finish in the 24-hour IEEE Xtreme.

achievements.heading: My first look at enterprise software
achievements.body: Zuari was my first look at enterprise software: on-premise SAP. I built a PHP dashboard, monitoring, and Python alerts.

achievements.heading: CyanogenMod for the Galaxy Ace
achievements.body: From 18 to 20, I worked on CyanogenMod for the Samsung Galaxy Ace in Southeast Asia. This was my idea of a hobby.

achievements.heading: School: CS, speaking, and leadership
achievements.body: At Navy Children School, I was house captain, found public speaking and debate, and finished Class 12 in the national top 0.01% for CS.

achievements.heading: Making the games I wanted to play
achievements.body: I kept making games: 3D Tic-Tac-Toe and a C++ Snake graphics project at GEC.

achievements.heading: Memory, context, and local AI
achievements.body: I gave my personal agent persistent memory with OpenMemory and Qdrant, and run local speech, image, and voice services on Apple Silicon.

achievements.heading: The Coldplay cameo
achievements.body: That's my silhouette at 3:41 in "In My Place." It also became my Gmail picture.

achievements.heading: Corporate awards are meaningless
achievements.body: I still kept the list: TMP All Star (top 1% of Salesforce contributors), Rising Star, SPOT, PEARL, Above and Beyond, and an AppSprint win.
